text:
Elliot Price: Trying to place the new “How to read our status page” content. Question: do we want it under Docs > Reliability, or as a top-level “Status” entry in the nav? Also need eyes on wording — don’t want to accidentally promise SLAs/response times.

Kira Thompson: +1 on wording. If it’s too buried, Support will keep linking a random KB. But if it’s top-level we need it to be super tight + not scary.

Rafael Mendes: For discoverability: customers will look in 2 places: (1) status page itself, (2) docs when searching. I’d put it in docs under a “Reliability / Incident communications” section and then add a short link from the status page footer (or “Subscribe” area) later.

Paula Mendes: Product angle: we’ve been saying “status page transparency upgrades” includes a public doc. Ideally the doc URL is stable and not buried 4 levels down.

Marissa Cole: Agree stable URL. Nav-wise: I’d avoid a new top-level item unless we’re ready to maintain it long term. Could do: Docs > Platform > Reliability > Status page.

Elliot Price: That works. I can create /reliability/status-page (or /reliability/status) as canonical, and we can decide later whether it shows in nav.

Kira Thompson: Copy question: what do we say about update frequency? We have internal cadence guidance by severity but we shouldn’t put “every 30 min” in public docs.

Rafael Mendes: Yep. We can say “we post an initial update as soon as we confirm customer impact, and we provide periodic updates while investigating/mitigating.” Use “aim to” / “typically” language. No hard numbers.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also avoid “SLA-backed” wording on the doc unless it’s explicitly the customer contract. The status page is best-effort comms.

Elliot Price: Proposed phrasing (draft): “During incidents, we aim to publish an initial status update promptly and continue to post periodic updates as we learn more.” Any objections?

Paula Mendes: Add: “Next update time” callout maybe? Since we’re enforcing it via incident-bot. But again, don’t promise specific intervals.

Kira Thompson: Maybe: “When possible, updates include when you can expect the next update.” That keeps it soft.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please also avoid “root cause details” commitments. Say we may share a category + mitigations, but we won’t publish sensitive details (security, customer-specific, provider confidential).

Michael Grant: +1 to Aisha. Also avoid language implying we’ll notify individual customers via email during every incident — that can create expectations. Stick to status page + support channels.

Elliot Price: Got it. Another area: “components” section. We’re adding granularity (Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank, Console, etc). We should explain that a component being degraded doesn’t necessarily mean full outage.

Rafael Mendes: That’s key. Include examples:
- “Streaming degraded” could be disconnects/timeouts but non-streaming responses still OK.
- Region component degraded could be isolated to us-east; customers can try pinning another region if configured.

Kira Thompson: Also include customer actions as “things to try”: retry with backoff, reduce concurrency, switch to non-streaming, fallback model. But keep it general and not a guaranteed fix.

Marissa Cole: Make sure we don’t recommend actions that conflict with Console UX / routing defaults. “If your integration supports it” prefacing helps.

Elliot Price: Plan: I’ll draft the doc in the docs repo and open a PR. I’ll tag @Rafael Mendes for technical accuracy and @Dr. Aisha Rahman / @Michael Grant for disclosure review.

Paula Mendes: Can you also include a small section: “What we do NOT publish” (no customer names, no prompt content, etc)? Support asked for something they can link.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. And explicitly: no vulnerability-level detail or exploitability info.

Sean Gallagher: One more: don’t say “post-incident summary within X days” as a guarantee. We can say “for major incidents, we usually publish a short summary after resolution.” Internally we’ll hold ourselves to the SLA.

Elliot Price: Makes sense. I’ll keep it as “usually” and “when available.”

Kira Thompson: Can we add a line that the status page reflects platform-wide components and may not represent the status of a customer’s private/on-prem deployment?

Rafael Mendes: Good call. Something like: “Private deployments may have separate operational status communicated through your support channel.”

Elliot Price: Action items:
- I’ll create /reliability/status-page as canonical URL
- Draft sections: components, incident phases (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved), what to expect, what we don’t share, common troubleshooting
- Review request once PR is up

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: please also drop the final URL in #support so they can update macros.

Elliot Price: Will do. PR by EOD tomorrow.

Michael Grant: When you have the draft, tag me before merge. Quick scan only, but want to ensure no accidental commitments.

Elliot Price: :white_check_mark: will tag.
